concerns.text: The research question and SC‑001 claim a causal relationship ('Student‑Only gating can replace the teacher‑student confidence gap') but the experimental design is purely comparative/observational and does not control for confounding factors, making the causal inference unsupported.

The plan does not specify a sufficient number of independent runs; earlier drafts indicated only 5 runs per variant (total 30 runs). This sample size yields low statistical power for detecting the claimed ≥60 % CPU‑time reduction and ≥80 % performance‑retention, even with bootstrapping.

Early‑stopping when the average reward reaches 0.8 causes the Student‑Only variant to terminate earlier than the Baseline, conflating per‑step CPU‑time reduction (SC‑002) with faster convergence. Comparing per‑step cost under differing episode counts introduces bias.

The fallback to a Kaggle T4 GPU if the model cannot load on CPU introduces a hardware confound: runs that switch to GPU will have different CPU‑time characteristics, violating the assumption that per‑step CPU cost is comparable across variants.
